notes:
I couldn't write any notes on Psalm 67 this time, because none of the sources loaded.

I tried to open seven pages in one go: Enduring Word, Gill, Ellicott and the Pulpit Commentary on Bible Hub, Precept Austin, Augustine on New Advent (Psalm 66 in his numbering), and the NET Bible notes. That request went over the tool's usage limit, and the tool then blocked any further calls for this turn. So I haven't read a single page.

Your rules say to report only what the pages say and to give a URL for every point. I'm not going to fill in the traditional reading, the differences between traditions, or Catholic, Orthodox and modern-scholarship views from memory, because none of it would be backed by a source.

If you send the request again, I'll open the pages one at a time to stay within the limit. I'd start with these, which are likely to give verse-by-verse comments:

- Enduring Word: enduringword.com/bible-commentary/psalm-67/
- Gill, Ellicott and the Pulpit Commentary: biblehub.com/commentaries/[gill|ellicott|pulpit]/psalms/67.htm
- Spurgeon's Treasury of David, on Bible Hub, StudyLight or spurgeon.org
- Precept Austin's Psalm 67 page
- NET Bible notes on Psalm 67
- Augustine on Psalm 67 (his Psalm 66) on newadvent.org
- Wesley's notes on wesley.nnu.edu, plus a look at gotquestions.org, ligonier.org and lcms.org for anything specific to a tradition

If you'd like the notes built up in stages, you could also ask for one or two sources per request.
